subject: lighthouse
pitch: A lighthouse on a tiny island.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a lighthouse scene using basic builder primitives: a rocky island base, a tapered tower, and other blocky stylized parts, keeping to safe, well-known API calls.

I'll add a single root joint for the island, then work out dimensions: a tower around 7m tall tapering from 1.1 to 0.7 radius, sitting atop a squashed sphere island roughly 3m wide, adjusting the island's vertical offset so it sinks slightly into the ground plane while the tower rests properly on top.

For the tower geometry, I'm leaning toward sweeping along a vertical path with a tapering radius and a modest number of sides for a stylized look, though I'm uncertain whether the sweep options support a direct "sides" parameter, so I'll check the spec before committing to an approach.

Then I'm planning the lighthouse's upper structure: a flat gallery deck with railing posts, a glass lantern room using a pale yellow tint, surrounding frame posts, and a dark red cone roof positioned above the lantern room to cap the whole tower.

I'm also sketching smaller details - a finial sphere at the roof's peak, a beacon light using a bright cylinder since emissive isn't an option, a dark wooden door embedded near the tower's base, and a small glowing window partway up. Finally I'm starting to design a stone keeper's cottage sitting elsewhere on the island, with light-colored walls.

Scattering small dodecahedron rocks across the island using a height function tied to the dome surface, then considering whether to add a flat water disc at ground level to represent the surrounding sea.

For the water, I'll size the cylinder so its top aligns with the floor and its radius exceeds the island's so it reads as a sea surrounding a tiny island. I'm also thinking about coloring the island using mottled paint blending rock and grass tones rather than a flat color, and weighing whether to add small wave details or keep things simple.

For a lighthouse touch, I'm debating adding a rotating light beam using an angled cone geometry extending from the lantern, but worried it might look odd without transparency—leaning toward including a simplified version anyway for character.

Writing imports...

I'm defining my color palette for the lighthouse scene—rock mottling, white and red stripes, glass, roof, wood, and water tones—then setting up the builder root joint for the island and starting the sphere geometry for the rocky base.

I'm figuring out how to flatten the sphere into an island shape with proper scaling, working out a height function to sample the terrain surface, and planning the tower's base position and vertical sweep path up from the island.

Now I'm sweeping a tapered cylindrical tower shape along that path with a tenagon cross-section, flat caps, and a red-and-white striped band pattern, then starting to add a cylindrical ring geometry at the top for the gallery.

Adding railing posts and a tilted torus rail, then building the lantern room as a glass cylinder with framing posts arranged around its circumference.

Now I'm layering the top cap ring, a conical roof, and a finial sphere, and reworking the lantern lighting since an opaque glass cylinder hides any inner glow—so I'll make the glass itself bright-colored with a lens ring detail instead of relying on an inner light source.

I'm placing the door box embedded into the tapering tower radius so its front face protrudes slightly, then computing window box positions using the tower's radius-as-a-function-of-height formula to keep them flush against the sloped wall at two different heights.

For the windows I'm generalizing to multiple compass angles, using rotation around Y to orient each window's outward face correctly. Then I'm sketching the cottage structure: wall box dimensions and center position, a four-sided pyramid roof sized to match the walls with 45-degree rotation, and a small door box on its front face.

Checking the cottage doesn't overlap the tower base much given their positions and radii, then I'm scattering rocks using dodecahedron shapes with randomized size and rotation, sinking them slightly into the terrain and rejecting any that fall too close to the cottage. Finally I'm adding a water disc using a flat cylinder positioned so its surface sits near ground level.

I'm adding a foam ring torus around the island edge, a scatter of flat box shapes as wave strokes on the water surface, skipping the light beam for simplicity, and confirming the single root joint works fine for all parts since there's only one bone. Then I'm sketching out the export structure with the meta object and default build function returning the root, making sure sweep paths and part placement default correctly to that single joint.

Writing stripe and helper code...
